topic: An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump
research_status: Museum and Commons research documented; actual V52B source painting/music exist in original artifact; 2019 gallery photo independently sourced and licensed, new MP4 pending

emotional_direction.central_tension: The white cockatoo is deprived of air in a scientific experiment, while the witnesses are divided between compassion, curiosity and indifference; Wright withholds the outcome.

evidence_details.observation: A rare white cockatoo is enclosed in a glass receiver connected to the air pump.
evidence_details.significance: Its uncertain fate transforms the scientific demonstration into a moral dilemma for the witnesses.

evidence_details.observation: The lecturer looks out toward the spectator while controlling the stopcock.
evidence_details.significance: The painting gives the demonstrator and the spectator responsibility for the bird's fate.

evidence_details.location: right side below the lecturer, girl hiding her face
evidence_details.observation: The elder girl covers her eyes; the younger child looks toward the experiment.
evidence_details.significance: Opposed responses turn the same event into terror for one person and fascination for another.

evidence_details.location: lower centre, rounded illuminated glass on table
evidence_details.observation: A candle is concealed behind a round vessel containing a diseased skull.
evidence_details.significance: The museum identifies a vanitas reminder of mortality and the limits of scientific knowledge.

evidence_details.location: upper right, boy by the window
evidence_details.observation: A boy waits holding the rope of the birdcage, whose role remains unresolved.
evidence_details.significance: The empty cage keeps open the possibility that the bird may return alive.

evidence_details.observation: The young couple are absorbed in each other instead of the air pump.
evidence_details.significance: Their indifference contrasts with the distress of the children and curiosity of other observers.

emotional_direction.opening_hook: The real painted cockatoo is visible immediately in its glass receiver, then the actual gilded museum frame provides physical context.
emotional_direction.closing_payoff: Return to the same historically photographed framed painting, leaving the bird's fate unresolved and the viewer implicated.
emotional_direction.wow_justification: The direct gaze of the lecturer and the frightened child turn an Enlightenment scientific scene into a moral choice, supported by National Gallery research.

critico_standard.variation_reason: Natural critical narration about science, spectators and morality with artwork details; no gallery entry

scenes.purpose: Present the real white cockatoo and the ethical stakes of the experiment
scenes.movement: Slow restrained study of authentic source pixels, no simulated life or edge stretching
scenes.spoken_line: Nel 1768 Joseph Wright dipinge un esperimento scientifico, ma la vera protagonista è la vita fragile di un cacatua bianco chiuso sotto una campana di vetro.

scenes.purpose: Read the lecturer's gesture and direct gaze as a challenge to the spectator
scenes.movement: Slow restrained study of authentic source pixels, no simulated life or edge stretching
scenes.spoken_line: Il dimostratore può continuare a togliere aria oppure riaprirla. Il suo sguardo ci coinvolge: non possiamo restare soltanto spettatori.

scenes.purpose: Compare the frightened and curious children without inventing movement
scenes.movement: Slow restrained study of authentic source pixels, no simulated life or edge stretching
scenes.spoken_line: La bambina più grande si copre il volto, mentre la più piccola osserva. Wright mette a confronto due reazioni umane alla stessa scena.

scenes.purpose: Explain the hidden candle and skull as a documented vanitas motif
scenes.movement: Slow restrained study of authentic source pixels, no simulated life or edge stretching
scenes.spoken_line: Una candela nascosta dietro il vetro illumina il tavolo e un teschio: il museo legge in questo dettaglio un richiamo alla mortalità.

scenes.purpose: Leave the boy's suspended birdcage as the unresolved dramatic question
scenes.movement: Slow restrained study of authentic source pixels, no simulated life or edge stretching
scenes.spoken_line: Il ragazzo vicino alla finestra tiene la corda della gabbia. Il dipinto non ci dice se l'uccello tornerà al suo posto.

scenes.purpose: Return to the scale of the canvas and the human range of reactions
scenes.movement: Slow restrained study of authentic source pixels, no simulated life or edge stretching
scenes.spoken_line: Con una tela di 183 per 244 centimetri, Wright trasforma una dimostrazione domestica in un grande teatro morale: sapere e compassione non coincidono sempre.
